entities.summary: Johann V Thurzo was a 15th-century Bishop of Wrocław in Silesia, now Poland. A great patron and lover of the arts and sciences, Martin Luther called him "the greatest bishop of the century". Thurzo was instrumental in the development of the University of Wrocław, which became a hub for humanist and Renaissance scholarship. He played a key role in the establishment of the Silesian Confederation, a regional alliance of cities and towns that opposed the growing power of the Polish king, Casimir IV. Thurzo's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he helped lay the groundwork for the Protestant Reformation in Silesia. His patronage of artists and scholars, including the famous artist Jan Polack, contributed to the region's rich cultural heritage. Thurzo's influence can still be felt today, as the city of Wrocław remains a center of learning and cultural activity.
